steps.name: QC: duplication, library-size outlier, compositional skew
caveats: High duplication in rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs is expected and is not on its own grounds to discard libraries or reads.
With 6 per group, a Wilcoxon test on QC metrics detects only very large group differences; a non-significant result is weak evidence of balance, not proof of it.
A single low-depth sample can dominate PC1 purely through the mean-variance relationship of log-CPM; interpret PCA on log-CPM with that in mind and do not read a library-size gradient as biology.
steps.context: Homo sapiens heart, bulk RNA-seq, raw gene-level Salmon counts, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, rRNA-depleted total RNA libraries WITHOUT UMIs. Sequencing QC reports >60% duplication in most libraries and sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. The duplication figure comes from the alignment QC, not from the count matrix, so it cannot be recomputed here — what CAN be computed from counts is the compositional skew that explains it. Without UMIs, duplicates are not separable from natural coverage saturation of high-abundance transcripts, so no deduplication is possible or appropriate; the question this step answers is whether the duplication is a uniform nuisance or a group-confounded artefact.
steps.question: In the 12-sample heart count matrix, does the >60% duplication rate differ systematically between treated and control, is it explained by transcriptome compositional skew typical of rRNA-depleted total RNA, and should sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) be retained in the treated-vs-control model?
constraints: Do NOT deduplicate, downsample, or subsample any library — the libraries have no UMIs and deduplication would preferentially deplete the genuinely highest-expressed cardiac and mitochondrial transcripts.
Keep the raw integer count matrix untouched as the input for downstream DE; this step writes QC tables and figures only, plus a plain-text/JSON verdict on sample_01.

Pre-specify the sample_01 decision rule and state it in the output BEFORE looking at any DE result: retain sample_01 in the primary model if its detected-gene count (counts >= 10) is within roughly 25% of the minimum of the other 11 samples and it does not sit as a lone extreme outlier on the sample-correlation heatmap; flag it for a leave-one-out sensitivity analysis regardless of the decision.
Report per-sample mitochondrial, residual-rRNA and top-100-gene fractions numerically in the QC table — these are the quantities that explain a high duplication rate in a total-RNA library.
State explicitly in the written output that duplication rate itself was not recomputed from counts and that the >60% figure is taken from the supplied sequencing QC.
steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-without-total-rna-highdup-n6-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 sample columns, first column gene symbol) and metadata.csv (12 rows, sample + condition). Produce a per-sample QC table: total counts, number of detected genes (count > 0 and count >= 10), the fraction of the library taken by the top 1/10/50/100 genes, the fraction assigned to mitochondrial genes (symbols matching ^MT-), to residual rRNA (symbols matching ^RNA5|^RNA18S|^RNA28S|^RNA45S|^RNA5-8S and MT-RNR1/MT-RNR2), and to the top cardiac structural genes present in the matrix (MYH7, MYH6, TNNT2, TNNI3, ACTC1, TPM1, MB, NPPA, DES, TTN). Test whether library size, detected-gene count, and top-N fraction differ between treated and control (Wilcoxon rank-sum, report effect size and note n=6 per group makes this a low-power check). Compute log-CPM, run PCA on the top 500 variable genes and hierarchical clustering on Spearman correlation of log-CPM, and report how much of PC1/PC2 associates with condition versus with log library size. Explicitly evaluate sample_01: its position in PCA/correlation space, its detected-gene count relative to the other 11, and its top-N fraction. Write a QC table CSV, a PCA plot, a sample-correlation heatmap, a library-size/complexity barplot, and a short written verdict on (a) whether duplication is plausibly natural given total-RNA composition or is group-confounded, and (b) whether sample_01 is retained.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample QC CSV covering all 12 samples with total counts, detected genes at two thresholds, top-1/10/50/100 fractions, MT fraction, residual rRNA fraction, and cardiac structural-gene fraction.

A statement of whether library size, complexity, or compositional skew differs between treated and control, with the test used and the acknowledgement that n=6 per group gives low power to detect such a difference.
PCA and sample-correlation heatmap figures produced, with PC1/PC2 association to condition and to log library size reported numerically.
An explicit, rule-based retain-or-drop verdict for sample_01, written down with the rule stated before the DE analysis runs.
No deduplicated or downsampled count matrix is produced or passed downstream.

steps.name: Primary DESeq2 treated vs control
caveats: Six versus six is modest power: genes with small effect sizes will not reach FDR significance, and absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change.
A p-value histogram that is not roughly uniform with a spike near zero signals a model problem (unmodelled structure, or a dominant outlier sample) and must be reported rather than ignored.

Median-of-ratios normalization assumes most genes are not differentially expressed; if the significant fraction is very large, or if a handful of cardiac structural genes take an extreme share of counts, note that the assumption is strained and let the T1S3 sensitivity analysis arbitrate.
steps.context: Human heart bulk RNA-seq, 12 samples, unpaired 6 vs 6, single batch — no covariates to model beyond condition. DESeq2's negative-binomial framework with per-sample size factors is the appropriate estimator at this sample size; median-of-ratios normalization handles the depth spread including sample_01 without any read-level correction. The high duplication rate is a property of the libraries, not of the count model, and requires no adjustment here provided T1S1 found it is not group-confounded.
steps.question: Which of the ~12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated and the 6 control human heart samples?
constraints: Use DESeq2 in R (version 1.52.0 is installed) with design ~ condition and an explicitly set reference level taken from the actual condition labels in metadata.csv — do not assume label spelling or ordering.
Verify that count-matrix column names and metadata sample identifiers match exactly and in order before constructing the DESeqDataSet; fail loudly on any mismatch rather than reindexing silently.
Apply independent filtering by pre-filtering to counts >= 10 in at least 6 samples, and let DESeq2's own independent filtering run on top; report both gene counts.
Report BOTH raw and apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes; use shrunken values for ranking and plotting, unshrunken with its standard error for any effect-size claim.
Use Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values; do not report nominal p-values as significant results.
If T1S1's verdict was to drop sample_01, run the primary model on 11 samples and say so prominently in every output; otherwise run all 12.
steps.description: Fit the primary differential expression model on the raw Salmon count matrix using DESeq2 with design ~ condition, contrast treated versus control (set control as the reference level explicitly from the metadata condition column; use the literal level names found in metadata.csv). Filter to genes with counts >= 10 in at least 6 samples (the size of the smaller group) before fitting, and report how many genes survive. Use median-of-ratios size factors and report them per sample alongside raw library size, so the effect of sample_01's low depth on its size factor is visible. Fit gene-wise dispersions with the standard shrinkage, produce the dispersion-estimate plot and the MA plot, and shrink log fold changes with apeglm for ranking. Report results with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR: full results table (gene symbol, baseMean, raw and shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) sorted by padj, plus counts of significant genes at padj < 0.05 and at padj < 0.05 with |shrunken log2FC| > 1. Produce a p-value histogram, a volcano plot labelling the top genes, and a heatmap of z-scored variance-stabilised counts for the top 50 genes by padj. Carry forward the sample_01 verdict from T1S1: run the primary model on whatever sample set that verdict specifies and state which it was.
acceptance_criteria: A full DE results table for every tested gene with gene symbol, baseMean, raw log2FC, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and BH padj.
Number of genes passing pre-filtering and number significant at padj < 0.05, reported separately from the count at padj < 0.05 plus |log2FC| > 1.
Dispersion plot, MA plot, p-value histogram, volcano plot and top-50 heatmap all produced.
Per-sample size factors reported next to raw library sizes, with sample_01 identifiable.
The sample set used (12 or 11) is stated explicitly and matches the T1S1 verdict.

steps.name: Robustness: leave-out sample_01 and limma-voom cross-check
caveats: Concordance between DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom is expected to be high because all three use closely related count models — agreement is a floor check, not independent validation.
A leave-one-out influence score is descriptive; with n=6 per group any single removal is a 17% change in group size, so some attrition is normal and does not by itself condemn a gene.
If dropping sample_01 changes the list substantially, the honest conclusion is that the study is underpowered for those genes, not that one of the two lists is correct.
steps.context: With 6 per group and one library at ~1/4 the median depth, a DE list can be driven by a single sample or by a normalization choice. This step exists to separate genes that are a property of the data from genes that are a property of the analysis decision. The total-RNA protocol makes the compositional check specifically relevant: a shift in residual rRNA or mitochondrial share between groups moves the size factors and can create apparent fold changes across many nuclear genes.
steps.question: Does the treated-versus-control gene list survive dropping the low-depth sample_01, and does an independent normalization and testing framework (limma-voom, and TMM-normalized edgeR quasi-likelihood) recover the same genes?
constraints: Use the same pre-filtering rule and the same contrast direction as T1S2 in every framework so the comparison is like-for-like.
Report concordance quantitatively: overlap counts, Jaccard index, and Spearman correlation of test statistics across the common gene set — not a Venn diagram alone.
The leave-one-out loop covers all 12 samples, not only sample_01.
Flag explicitly any gene in the primary top list that is mitochondrial (MT-) or rRNA-derived, and state that such a change may be compositional rather than regulatory.
Do not redefine the primary result — this step annotates and stress-tests T1S2's list; the headline DE answer remains T1S2's.
steps.description: Run two sensitivity analyses against the T1S2 primary result and report their concordance. (a) Leave-one-out: refit the same DESeq2 model on the sample set that EXCLUDES sample_01 (or, if T1S1 already excluded it, refit on all 12 to show what its inclusion would have done), and additionally run a full leave-one-sample-out loop over all 12 samples recording, for each of the primary top 100 genes, how many of the 12 refits keep it at padj < 0.05 — an influence score per gene. (b) Independent framework: run limma-voom with TMM normalization and, separately, edgeR quasi-likelihood F-tests on the same filtered matrix and contrast. Compare the three primary gene lists by overlap at padj < 0.05, by Spearman correlation of the test statistics across all tested genes, and with a rank-rank scatter. Emit a consolidated table of genes that are significant in the primary DESeq2 analysis, annotated with: significance under limma-voom, significance under edgeR-QLF, leave-one-out influence score, and a boolean 'robust' flag for genes significant in all three frameworks and in at least 10 of 12 leave-one-out refits. Report the residual-rRNA and mitochondrial fraction per sample from T1S1 alongside, and state whether any top gene is itself a mitochondrial or rRNA-derived feature whose apparent change could reflect compositional shift rather than regulation.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated per-gene table for all primary padj < 0.05 genes carrying limma-voom and edgeR-QLF significance, a leave-one-out influence score out of 12, and a robust flag.
Numeric concordance between DESeq2, limma-voom and edgeR-QLF: significant-gene overlap, Jaccard, and Spearman correlation of statistics.
An explicit statement of how many primary significant genes are lost when sample_01 is excluded (or gained when it is included), by name where the count is small.
Mitochondrial and rRNA-derived features among the top genes are identified and annotated as potentially compositional.

steps.name: GSEA on the ranked treated-vs-control statistic
caveats: GSEA on a 6v6 contrast inherits that contrast's noise; a strong NES on a weakly-separated ranking is not strong evidence.
GO sets are nested and hits arrive in correlated blocks — reporting the raw number of significant terms overstates the number of independent findings.

In total-RNA heart libraries, oxidative-phosphorylation and ribosomal set enrichment can reflect residual compositional differences in the libraries rather than regulation; cross-check any such hit against the per-sample MT and rRNA fractions from T1S1 before interpreting it biologically.
steps.context: Interpretation layer for the treated-versus-control contrast in human heart tissue. The reference store visible at planning time holds human hallmark, GO BP/CC/MF, KEGG MEDICUS, BioCarta and PID GMTs keyed by HGNC symbol, matching the count matrix's gene-symbol identifiers. This step enriches the answer but is not required to answer the research question — the DE result stands on its own.
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are coordinately shifted between treated and control heart samples, given the full ranked DESeq2 statistic rather than a thresholded gene list?
constraints: Resolve human gene-set collections from the environment's reference store at run time; use human sets only, never the mouse GMTs, since the data is Homo sapiens.

If a collection cannot be resolved at run time, report which one is missing and proceed with whichever human collections are present; if none is available, report that the enrichment step could not run and do not substitute an ad-hoc or hard-coded gene set.
Rank the FULL tested gene list, not only significant genes — pre-ranked GSEA is the primary enrichment method here precisely because the 6v6 design may yield few FDR-significant genes.
Report the fraction of ranked genes that match each collection's symbol space before interpreting any result.
Report BH-adjusted p-values across all sets tested within each collection, and collapse redundant nested GO terms before quoting a number of enriched processes.
Run the over-representation test only if the T1S3 robust list has at least 10 genes in a direction; otherwise report GSEA alone and say why.
steps.description: Take the complete T1S2 DESeq2 result, rank all tested genes by the Wald statistic (or by -log10(pvalue) signed by the shrunken log2FC where the statistic is unavailable), and run pre-ranked GSEA with fgsea against human gene-set collections resolved from the environment's reference store: the hallmark collection, the GO Biological Process branch, and the curated canonical pathway collections (KEGG MEDICUS, BioCarta, PID). Human HGNC symbols are the identifier space in both the count matrix and these GMTs, so no ID conversion should be needed — verify the overlap between matrix symbols and set members and report the match rate before testing. Restrict to sets of 15-500 genes, use at least 10000 permutations or the fgsea multilevel procedure, and report normalised enrichment scores with BH-adjusted p-values. Collapse redundant parent/child GO hits before reporting a count. Additionally run an over-representation test on the T1S3 'robust' significant gene list (up and down separately) against the same collections, using the tested-gene universe from T1S2 as background. Produce a table of significant sets with NES, padj, set size and leading-edge genes, plus enrichment plots for the top sets and a summary figure. Given heart tissue, note separately whether any enriched set is dominated by sarcomeric, mitochondrial-oxidative-phosphorylation, or fibrotic gene membership.
acceptance_criteria: A table of enriched gene sets per collection with NES, nominal p, BH padj, set size and leading-edge gene symbols.
The symbol match rate between the ranked gene list and each collection is reported.
Redundant GO parent/child hits are collapsed before any count of enriched processes is quoted.
Enrichment plots for the top sets and a summary figure are produced.
If a collection was absent at run time, the step's output names it explicitly rather than silently omitting it.

plan.title: Treated vs control heart bulk RNA-seq DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a straightforward two-group differential expression on 12 human heart bulk RNA-seq libraries (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) with a 12000 x 13 Salmon gene-level count matrix keyed by gene symbol. Two data-specific facts drive the plan. (1) The QC flags >60% duplication in most libraries. For rRNA-depleted total RNA libraries without UMIs, high duplication is expected and is NOT by itself evidence of PCR-artefact bias: total RNA protocols sequence a compact, highly-skewed transcriptome (residual rRNA, mitochondrial transcripts, and in heart a handful of sarcomeric genes such as MYH7, TNNT2, ACTC1, MB that can occupy a large fraction of reads), so duplicate reads are largely natural duplicates from high-abundance transcripts. With no UMIs, duplicates cannot be distinguished from natural coverage saturation, and deduplication would bias exactly the highest-expressed genes. So the plan does not deduplicate; instead T1S1 quantifies whether duplication tracks library complexity in a way that differs BETWEEN groups (a group-confounded technical artefact would invalidate the contrast) versus uniformly (a nuisance that count-based modelling absorbs). It also quantifies the rRNA/mito/top-gene fraction per sample, which is the actual driver of effective library size in total RNA data. (2) sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which for a 6v6 design is the single biggest threat to power and to the dispersion fit; T1S1 decides its fate on stated, pre-specified criteria rather than by eyeballing the volcano. T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 negative-binomial contrast (treated vs control) on the full 12-sample set with median-of-ratios normalization, which is robust to the compositional skew total RNA induces provided no single gene dominates; T1S3 repeats it without sample_01 and as a limma-voom sensitivity check so the reported gene list is the one stable across normalization and sample-inclusion choices, not an artefact of either. T1S4 takes the ranked statistic into hallmark/GO/canonical-pathway GSEA for interpretation. Enrichment is downstream and optional to the core question: if the pathway GMTs are missing at run time, the DE result still answers the question in full.

Do not redefine the primary result — this step annotates and stress-tests T1S2's list; the headline DE answer remains T1S2's.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated per-gene table for all primary padj < 0.05 genes carrying limma-voom and edgeR-QLF significance, a leave-one-out influence score out of 12, and a robust flag.
Numeric concordance between DESeq2, limma-voom and edgeR-QLF: significant-gene overlap, Jaccard, and Spearman correlation of statistics.
An explicit statement of how many primary significant genes are lost when sample_01 is excluded (or gained when it is included), by name where the count is small.
Mitochondrial and rRNA-derived features among the top genes are identified and annotated as potentially compositional.
caveats: Concordance between DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom is expected to be high because all three use closely related count models — agreement is a floor check, not independent validation.
A leave-one-out influence score is descriptive; with n=6 per group any single removal is a 17% change in group size, so some attrition is normal and does not by itself condemn a gene.
If dropping sample_01 changes the list substantially, the honest conclusion is that the study is underpowered for those genes, not that one of the two lists is correct.

steps.name: GSEA on the ranked treated-vs-control statistic
steps.question: Which biological processes and pathways are coordinately shifted between treated and control heart samples, given the full ranked DESeq2 statistic rather than a thresholded gene list?
steps.description: Take the complete T1S2 DESeq2 result, rank all tested genes by the Wald statistic (or by -log10(pvalue) signed by the shrunken log2FC where the statistic is unavailable), and run pre-ranked GSEA with fgsea against human gene-set collections resolved from the environment's reference store: the hallmark collection, the GO Biological Process branch, and the curated canonical pathway collections (KEGG MEDICUS, BioCarta, PID). Human HGNC symbols are the identifier space in both the count matrix and these GMTs, so no ID conversion should be needed — verify the overlap between matrix symbols and set members and report the match rate before testing. Restrict to sets of 15-500 genes, use at least 10000 permutations or the fgsea multilevel procedure, and report normalised enrichment scores with BH-adjusted p-values. Collapse redundant parent/child GO hits before reporting a count. Additionally run an over-representation test on the T1S3 'robust' significant gene list (up and down separately) against the same collections, using the tested-gene universe from T1S2 as background. Produce a table of significant sets with NES, padj, set size and leading-edge genes, plus enrichment plots for the top sets and a summary figure. Given heart tissue, note separately whether any enriched set is dominated by sarcomeric, mitochondrial-oxidative-phosphorylation, or fibrotic gene membership.
steps.context: Interpretation layer for the treated-versus-control contrast in human heart tissue. The reference store visible at planning time holds human hallmark, GO BP/CC/MF, KEGG MEDICUS, BioCarta and PID GMTs keyed by HGNC symbol, matching the count matrix's gene-symbol identifiers. This step enriches the answer but is not required to answer the research question — the DE result stands on its own.
constraints: Resolve human gene-set collections from the environment's reference store at run time; use human sets only, never the mouse GMTs, since the data is Homo sapiens.

If a collection cannot be resolved at run time, report which one is missing and proceed with whichever human collections are present; if none is available, report that the enrichment step could not run and do not substitute an ad-hoc or hard-coded gene set.
Rank the FULL tested gene list, not only significant genes — pre-ranked GSEA is the primary enrichment method here precisely because the 6v6 design may yield few FDR-significant genes.
Report the fraction of ranked genes that match each collection's symbol space before interpreting any result.
Report BH-adjusted p-values across all sets tested within each collection, and collapse redundant nested GO terms before quoting a number of enriched processes.
Run the over-representation test only if the T1S3 robust list has at least 10 genes in a direction; otherwise report GSEA alone and say why.
acceptance_criteria: A table of enriched gene sets per collection with NES, nominal p, BH padj, set size and leading-edge gene symbols.
The symbol match rate between the ranked gene list and each collection is reported.
Redundant GO parent/child hits are collapsed before any count of enriched processes is quoted.
Enrichment plots for the top sets and a summary figure are produced.
If a collection was absent at run time, the step's output names it explicitly rather than silently omitting it.
caveats: GSEA on a 6v6 contrast inherits that contrast's noise; a strong NES on a weakly-separated ranking is not strong evidence.
GO sets are nested and hits arrive in correlated blocks — reporting the raw number of significant terms overstates the number of independent findings.

In total-RNA heart libraries, oxidative-phosphorylation and ribosomal set enrichment can reflect residual compositional differences in the libraries rather than regulation; cross-check any such hit against the per-sample MT and rRNA fractions from T1S1 before interpreting it biologically.
